title: حِكَايَةُ الصَّيَّادِ
titleEn: The Story of the Fisherman, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 38–41 (continuing directly from nights-05, whose text ends with the fisherman renewing his plea to the trapped efrit), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the project’s own two-pass-plus-adjudication pipeline; the edition’s own OCR is unusable. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition’s — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms and a few genuinely obscure or compositor’s-slip-looking words, is preserved unaltered; such forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized automatically once this file is published, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 6 closes the fisherman’s encounter with the efrit he trapped in a sealed copper jar (begun on Night 3, and held in suspense through the two embedded tales of Nights 4–5): bound by the oath the fisherman exacts and moved by the very precedent of the King Yunan and Duban story he has just told, the efrit is released, flings the jar itself into the sea, and leads the fisherman to a remote pool where he may catch fish of four colors — but only once a day — before sinking into the earth himself, his own part in the frame now finished. The fisherman brings the fish to the Sultan as a gift; when the palace cook fries them, the kitchen wall splits open, a bejewelled maiden emerges with a wand and addresses the fish in verse, they answer her in kind, and all four are found burnt to charcoal. The astonished vizier has the whole scene repeated before his own eyes with a second catch of fish, with the same result — setting up the longer, stranger tale the Sultan will pursue in nights to come. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language toward Classical Arabic here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit. The night is frank about its own moments of violence and dread and is translated that way.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ قَالَتْ لَهَا أُخْتُهَا دُنْيَازَادُ إِنَّنِي لَهَا حَدِيثُكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu qālat lahā ukhtuhā dunyāzādu innanī lahā ḥadīthuki
sentences.l: So when it was the sixth night, her sister Dunyazad said to her, "Indeed I — for it — your story!"
sentences.i: Now when the sixth night came, her sister Dunyazad said to her, "Truly, I am eager for it — your story!"
sentences.n: The phrase "innanī lahā ḥadīthuki" is elliptical; elsewhere the frame formula has Dunyazad ask her sister to finish the story. Here "lahā" (lit. "for it") seems to work idiomatically for eagerness/attachment ("I'm keen for it"), with "your story" standing in apposition. The reading is uncertain and rendered by best evident sense.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنْ أَذِنَ لِي الْمَلِكُ فَقَالَ لَهَا قُولِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat in adhina lī al-maliku fa-qāla lahā qūlī
sentences.l: So she said, "If the king gives me permission." So he said to her, "Say (it)."
sentences.i: She said, "If the king gives me leave." And he said to her, "Speak."

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الصَّيَّادَ قَٰلَ لِلْعِفْرِيتِ لَوْ أَبْقَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ أَبْقَيْتُكَ لَٰكِنْ مَا أَرَدْتَ إِلَّا قَتْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-ṣayyāda qāla li-al-ʿifrīti law abqaytanī kuntu abqaytuka lākin mā aradta illā qatlī
sentences.l: So she said, "It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the fisherman said to the efrit: If you had spared me, I would have spared you, but you wanted nothing but my killing."
sentences.i: She said, "It has reached me, O fortunate King, that the fisherman said to the efrit: Had you spared me, I would have spared you; but you wanted nothing except to kill me."
sentences.n: Printed "قل" for "قال" (defective, missing its alif); pointed here with a dagger alif (قَٰلَ) to preserve the rasm while giving the Classical reading qāla. This spelling recurs for qāla throughout the edition.

sentences.t: فَهَا أَنَا أَقْتُلُكَ بِحَبْسِكَ فِي هَٰذَا الْقُمْقُمِ وَأُلْقِيكَ فِي هَٰذَا الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-hā anā aqtuluka bi-ḥabsika fī hādhā al-qumqumi wa-ulqīka fī hādhā al-baḥri
sentences.l: So here I am, killing you, by imprisoning you in this jar and casting you into this sea.
sentences.i: So now, I will kill you — by shutting you up in this jar and throwing you into this sea.

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ الْمَارِدُ وَ قَالَ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا الصَّيَّادُ لَا تَفْعَلْ وَ أَبْقِنِي أَنْتَ وَ لَا تُوَاخِذْنِي بِعَمَلِي فَإِذَا كُنْتُ أَنَا مُسِيًا كُنْ أَنْتَ مُحْسِنًا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha al-māridu wa-qāla bi-Allāhi ʿalayka ayyuhā al-ṣayyādu lā tafʿal wa-abqinī anta wa-lā tuwākhidhnī bi-ʿamalī fa-idhā kuntu anā musiyan kun anta muḥsinan
sentences.l: So the demon cried out and said, "By God, upon you, O fisherman — do not do (it); spare me, you, and do not blame me for my deed. So if I was a wrongdoer, you be a doer of good."
sentences.i: The demon cried out and said, "By God, I beg you, fisherman — do not do this! Spare me, and do not hold my past deed against me. If I was the wrongdoer, be you the one who does good."
sentences.n: "تواخذني" is spelled with wāw rather than the expected hamza (تؤاخذني, "you hold me to account"); kept as printed and read tuwākhidhnī. "مسيا" stands for مُسِيء ("one who does wrong"), spelled here without its hamza letter — read musiyan.

sentences.t: وَ فِي الْأَمْثَالِ السَّايِرَةِ يَا مُحْسِنُ لِمَنْ أَسَاءَ كَفَى الْمُسِئَ فِعْلُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-amthāli al-sāyirati yā muḥsinu li-man asāʾa kafā al-musīʾa fiʿluhu
sentences.l: And among the current proverbs: "O one who does good to him who does evil — the wrongdoer's own deed is enough for him."
sentences.i: And among the well-known proverbs: "O you who are kind to one who does wrong — the wrongdoer's own deed is punishment enough for him."
sentences.n: "السايرة" stands for السَّائِرَة ("current, well-known [proverbs]"), spelled here with yā in place of hamza. "المسئ" stands for المُسِيء ("the wrongdoer"), here spelled without the internal yā, but its hamza letter (ئ) is printed and kept as such.

sentences.t: وَ لَا تَعْمَلْ كَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَمَانَةً مَعَ عَائِكَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā taʿmal kamā ʿalimta amānatan maʿa ʿāʾikata
sentences.l: And do not do as you know [was done] — a good turn — with ʿĀʾika.
sentences.i: Do not repay me as, you well know, a kindness was once repaid — in the case of ʿĀʾika.
sentences.n: "عائكة" is obscure: its identity, and even whether its reading is secure, are uncertain. It may be a proper name (person, animal, or place) belonging to a proverb about a kindness repaid with harm, imperfectly preserved here; rendered by its most evident phonetic value. The fisherman's reply in the next line, asking what this refers to, suggests the reference was already puzzling within the story itself.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّيَّادُ وَمَا عَمِلْتَ أَمَانَةً مَعَ عَائِكَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣayyādu wa-mā ʿamilta amānatan maʿa ʿāʾikata
sentences.l: So the fisherman said, "But what good turn did I do with ʿĀʾika?"
sentences.i: The fisherman said, "But what kindness did I ever do concerning ʿĀʾika?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعِفْرِيتُ مَا هَٰذَا وَقْتَ حَدِيثٍ وَ أَنَا فِي هَٰذَا السِّجْنِ حَتَّى تُطْلِقَنِي وَ أَنَا أُحَدِّثُكَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿifrītu mā hādhā waqta ḥadīthin wa-anā fī hādhā al-sijni ḥattā tuṭliqanī wa-anā uḥaddithuka bihi
sentences.l: So the efrit said, "This is not the time for a story, while I am in this prison — until you release me, then I will tell it to you."
sentences.i: The efrit said, "This is no time for storytelling, with me still shut in this prison. Release me, and I will tell it to you."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّيَّادُ خَلِّ عَنْكَ هَٰذَا الْكَلَامَ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ إِلْقَائِكَ فِي الْبَحْرِ وَ لَا سَبِيلَ إِلَى إِخْرَاجِكَ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣayyādu khalli ʿanka hādhā al-kalāma lā budda min ilqāʾika fī al-baḥri wa-lā sabīla ilā ikhrājika abadan
sentences.l: So the fisherman said, "Leave off this talk — there is no escape from your being cast into the sea, and there is no way to your release, ever."
sentences.i: The fisherman said, "Enough of this talk! You must be cast into the sea, and there is no way to get you out, ever."

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي كُنْتُ أَتَدَخَّلُ عَلَيْكَ وَأَتَضَرَّعُ إِلَيْكَ وَ أَنْتَ لَا تُرِيدُ إِلَّا قَتْلِي بِغَيْرِ ذَنْبٍ اِسْتَوْجَبَهُ مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innī kuntu atadakhkhalu ʿalayka wa-ataḍarraʿu ilayka wa-anta lā turīdu illā qatlī bi-ghayri dhanbin istawjabahu minka
sentences.l: For indeed, I used to come in upon you and plead with you, while you want nothing but my killing, without a sin that would deserve it from you.
sentences.i: For I used to come to you and plead with you, yet you want nothing but to kill me, though I have committed no offense that would earn this from you.

sentences.t: وَ لَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَكَ سُوءًا أَبَدًا وَ إِنِّي مَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَكَ إِلَّا خَيْرًا لِكَوْنِي أَخْرَجْتُكَ مِنَ السِّجْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā faʿaltu maʿaka sūʾan abadan wa-innī mā faʿaltu maʿaka illā khayran li-kawnī akhrajtuka mina al-sijni
sentences.l: And I did not do with you any evil, ever; and indeed I did with you nothing but good, in that I took you out of the prison.
sentences.i: And I never did you any harm at all; indeed, I did you nothing but good, in that I freed you from the prison.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَعَلْتَ مَعِي ذَٰلِكَ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكَ رَدِيُّ الْفِعْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faʿalta maʿī dhālika ʿalimtu annaka radiyyu al-fiʿli
sentences.l: So when you did that with me, I knew that you are evil of deed.
sentences.i: So when you did that to me, I knew you for one whose deeds are evil.
sentences.n: "ردي" stands for رَدِيء ("bad, evil"), spelled here without its final hamza letter, as elsewhere in this passage (cf. مسيا, السايرة); pointed radiyy- to preserve the rasm.

sentences.t: وَ اِعْلَمْ أَنِّي إِذَا رَمَيْتُكَ فِي هَٰذَا الْبَحْرِ لِأَجْلِ كُلِّ مَنْ ظَلَمَكَ يَرْمِيكَ ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam annī idhā ramaytuka fī hādhā al-baḥri li-ajli kulli man ẕalamaka yarmīka thāniya marratin
sentences.l: And know that I, if I cast you into this sea, for the sake of everyone you have wronged, [whoever finds you] will cast you in a second time.
sentences.i: And know this: even if I do cast you into this sea, it is for the sake of everyone you have wronged — whoever comes after me will cast you back in a second time.
sentences.n: The referent of "-ka" in "ẕalamaka"/"yarmīka" is ambiguous — it could denote a generic future victim of the efrit rather than a specific past wrong done to him; rendered here by the sense that best fits the fisherman's following threat to warn others.

sentences.t: أُخْبِرُهُ بِمَا جَرَى لِي مَعَكَ وَأُحَذِّرُهُ وَتُقِيمُ فِي هَٰذَا الْبَحْرِ إِلَى أٰخِرِ الزَّمَانِ حَتَّى تَهْلِكَ
sentences.tr: ukhbiruhu bimā jarā lī maʿaka wa-uḥadhdhiruhu wa-taqīmu fī hādhā al-baḥri ilā ākhiri al-zamāni ḥattā tahlika
sentences.l: I will tell him what happened to me with you, and I will warn him; and you will remain in this sea until the end of time, until you perish.
sentences.i: I will tell him what passed between us and put him on his guard against you; and you will stay in this sea until the end of time, until you perish.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ أَطْلِقْنِي
sentences.tr: qāla lahu al-ʿifrītu aṭliqnī
sentences.l: The efrit said to him, "Release me."

sentences.t: فَهٰذَا وَقْتُ الْمُرُوءَةِ وَ أَنَا أُعَاهِدُكَ لَمْ أَعْصِ عَلَيْكَ أَبَدًا وَ أَنْفَعُكَ بِشَيْءٍ يُغْنِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā waqtu al-murūʾati wa-anā uʿāhiduka lam aʿṣi ʿalayka abadan wa-anfaʿuka bi-shayʾin yughnīka
sentences.l: So this is the time of manly virtue, and I make a covenant with you: I will never disobey you, and I will benefit you with something that will content you.
sentences.i: This, then, is the moment for nobility of soul. I pledge myself to you: I will never disobey you, and I will do you a good turn that will satisfy your needs.
sentences.n: Continues the efrit's speech from the end of the previous night, as he asks the fisherman to let him out of the jar.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَأَخَذَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّيَّادُ الْعَهْدَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا أَطْلَقَهُ لَا يُوذِيهِ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ يَعْمَلُ مَعَهُ الْجَمِيلَ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-akhadha ʿalayhi al-ṣayyādu al-ʿahda annahu idhā aṭlaqahu lā yūdhīhi illā annahu yaʿmalu maʿahu al-jamīla
sentences.l: He said: So the fisherman took from him the covenant that, if he released him, he would not harm him, but rather that he would do him good.
sentences.i: So: the fisherman bound him by a covenant that, once set free, he would do him no harm, but would instead deal kindly with him.
sentences.n: The opening qāla ('he said') is the storyteller's formula resuming the narration, not a new speaker. يوذيه reflects Classical يؤذيه with its hamza smoothed onto a plain wāw, as this text often does with medial hamzas.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ وَ حَلَفَهُ بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمِ فَتَحَ لَهُ الصَّيَّادُ الْقُمْقُمَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istawthaqa minhu wa-ḥalafahu bi-ismi Allāhi al-aʿẕami fataḥa lahu al-ṣayyādu al-qumquma
sentences.l: Then when he had made sure of him, and made him swear by the Greatest Name of God, the fisherman opened the jar for him.
sentences.i: When he had thus secured his word, making him swear by God's Greatest Name, the fisherman opened the jar for him.

sentences.t: فَتَصَاعَدَ الدُّخَانُ حَتَّى خَرَجَ وَ تَكَامَلَ فَصَارَ عِفْرِيتًا سَوِيًّا
sentences.tr: fa-taṣāʿada al-dukhānu ḥattā kharaja wa-takāmala fa-ṣāra ʿifrītan sawiyyan
sentences.l: Then the smoke rose up until it came out and became whole, and it became a well-formed efrit.
sentences.i: The smoke rose and rose until it had wholly emerged and taken shape, becoming an efrit whole and well-formed.

sentences.t: فَرَفَسَ الْقُمْقُمَ رَمَاهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ فَلَمَّا رَأهُ الصَّيَّادُ رَمَى الْقُمْقُمَ فِي الْبَحْرِ أَيْقَنَ بِالْهَلَاكِ وَ شَرْشَرَ فِي ثِيَابِهِ وَ قَالَ هٰذِهِ لَيْسَتْ عَلَامَةَ خَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-rafasa al-qumquma ramāhu fī al-baḥri fa-lammā raʾāhu al-ṣayyādu ramā al-qumquma fī al-baḥri ayqana bi-al-halāki wa-sharshara fī thiyābihi wa-qāla hādhihi laysat ʿalāmata khayrin
sentences.l: Then he kicked the jar, throwing it into the sea; and when the fisherman saw him throw the jar into the sea, he became certain of ruin, and tore at his clothes, and said, 'This is not a sign of good.'
sentences.i: He kicked the jar and flung it into the sea; and when the fisherman saw the jar thrown into the sea, he felt sure of his own destruction, and tore at his clothes, saying, 'This is no good omen.'
sentences.n: شرشر is a rare, expressive verb meaning to rend or tear repeatedly, here of tearing at one's own clothes in distress.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَوِيَ قَلْبُهُ وَ قَالَ أَيُّهَا الْعِفْرِيتُ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسُولًا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qawiya qalbuhu wa-qāla ayyuhā al-ʿifrītu qāla Allāhu taʿālā awfū bi-al-ʿahdi inna al-ʿahda kāna masūlan
sentences.l: Then his heart grew strong, and he said, 'O efrit, God Most High has said: Fulfil the covenant; indeed the covenant shall be asked about.'
sentences.i: Then he took heart, and said, 'O efrit, God Most High has said: Fulfil the covenant, for the covenant shall be called to account.'
sentences.n: Quotes Qur'an 17:34 (wa-awfū bi-al-ʿahdi inna al-ʿahda kāna masʾūlan, 'and fulfil the covenant, for the covenant shall be asked about'). This text spells the last word مسولا, smoothing the Qur'anic medial hamza (masʾūlan) into a plain wāw (masūlan), as it does elsewhere.

sentences.t: وَ أَنْتَ قَدْ عَاهَدْتَنِي وَ حَلَفْتَ أَنَّكَ لَمْ تَغْدُرْنِي يَغْدُرْكَ اللَّهُ فَإِنَّهُ غَيُورٌ يُمْهِلُ وَ لَا يُهْمِلُ
sentences.tr: wa-anta qad ʿāhadtanī wa-ḥalafta annaka lam taghdurnī yaghdurka Allāhu fa-innahu ghayūrun yumhilu wa-lā yuhmilu
sentences.l: And you have made a covenant with me, and sworn that you would not betray me — may God betray you (if you do); for He is jealous: He grants delay but does not neglect.
sentences.i: You have pledged yourself to me and sworn that you would not betray me — and if you do, may God betray you; for He is a jealous guardian who may grant delay, but never overlooks a wrong.
sentences.n: يمهل ولا يهمل is a well-known proverbial phrase about divine justice: God may postpone retribution, but never forgets it.

sentences.t: وَ أَنَا قُلْتُ لَكَ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ الْحَكِيمُ دُوبَانُ لِلْمَلِكِ يُونَانَ أَبْقِنِي يُبْقِكَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā qultu laka mithla mā qāla al-ḥakīmu Dūbānu li-al-maliki Yūnāna abqinī yubqika Allāhu
sentences.l: And I have said to you the like of what the sage Duban said to King Yunan: 'Spare me, and God will spare you.'
sentences.i: And I say to you what the sage Duban once said to King Yunan: 'Spare me, and may God spare you.'
sentences.n: A reference back to the tale of the sage Duban and King Yunan, told over the preceding nights; it is quoted here only as a proverbial saying, not retold.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْعِفْرِيتُ وَ مَشَى قُدَّامَهُ وَ قَالَ أَيُّهَا الصَّيَّادُ اتَّبِعْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-ʿifrītu wa-mashā quddāmahu wa-qāla ayyuhā al-ṣayyādu itbaʿnī
sentences.l: Then the efrit laughed, and walked ahead of him, and said, 'O fisherman, follow me.'

sentences.t: فَمَشَى الصَّيَّادُ وَرَاءَهُ وَ هُوَ لَمْ يُصَدِّقْ بِالنَّجَاةِ وَ مَشَى إِلَى أَنْ خَرَجُوا إِلَى ظَاهِرِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَ طَلَعَ إِلَى جَبَلٍ وَ نَزَلَ إِلَى بَرِّيَّةٍ مُتَّسِعَةٍ وَ إِذَا هُمَا بِبِرْكَةِ مَاءٍ فَنَزَلَ فِي وَسَطِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-mashā al-ṣayyādu warāʾahu wa-huwa lam yuṣaddiq bi-al-najāti wa-mashā ilā an kharajū ilā ẕāhiri al-madīnati wa-ṭalaʿa ilā jabalin wa-nazala ilā barriyyatin muttasiʿatin wa-idhā humā bi-birkati māʾin fa-nazala fī wasaṭihā
sentences.l: So the fisherman walked behind him, not believing in his own deliverance; and he walked on until they went out to the outskirts of the city, and went up onto a mountain, and went down into a wide wilderness, and, behold, the two of them were at a pool of water; and he went down into the middle of it.
sentences.i: The fisherman walked behind him, scarcely able to believe he had truly been saved, until they came out to the edge of the city, climbed a mountain, and went down into a broad wasteland, where suddenly they came upon a pool of water; and the efrit went down into the middle of it.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَ لِلصَّيَّادِ اتَّبِعْنِي فَتَبِعَهُ إِلَى وَسَطِ الْبِرْكَةِ فَوَقَفَ الْعِفْرِيتُ وَ أَمَرَ الصَّيَّادَ أَنْ يَطْرَحَ الشَّبَكَةَ وَ يَصْطَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-ṣayyādi itbaʿnī fa-tabiʿahu ilā wasaṭi al-birkati fa-waqafa al-ʿifrītu wa-amara al-ṣayyāda an yaṭraḥa al-shabakata wa-yaṣṭāda
sentences.l: And he said to the fisherman, 'Follow me'; so he followed him to the middle of the pool; then the efrit stopped, and ordered the fisherman to cast the net and fish.
sentences.i: He said to the fisherman, 'Follow me'; so the fisherman followed him to the middle of the pool. There the efrit stopped, and told him to cast his net and fish.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الصَّيَّادُ إِلَى الْبِرْكَةِ فَرَأَى فِيهَا السَّمَكَ الْمُلَوَّنَ الْأَبْيَضَ وَ الْأَحْمَرَ وَ الْأَزْرَقَ وَ الْأَصْفَرَ فَتَعَجَّبَ الصَّيَّادُ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-naẕara al-ṣayyādu ilā al-birkati fa-raʾā fīhā al-samaka al-mulawwana al-abyaḍa wa-al-aḥmara wa-al-azraqa wa-al-aṣfara fa-taʿajjaba al-ṣayyādu min dhālika
sentences.l: Then the fisherman looked at the pool, and saw in it colored fish — white, and red, and blue, and yellow; and the fisherman marveled at that.
sentences.i: The fisherman looked into the pool and saw fish of many colors in it — white, red, blue and yellow — and he marveled at it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَخْرَجَ شَبَكَتَهُ وَ طَرَحَهَا وَ جَذَبَهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا أَرْبَعَ سَمَكَاتٍ كُلٌّ بِلَوْنٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu akhraja shabakatahu wa-ṭaraḥahā wa-jadhabahā fa-wajada fīhā arbaʿa samakātin kullun bi-lawnin
sentences.l: Then he took out his net, and cast it, and drew it in, and found in it four fish, each of a (different) color.
sentences.i: Then he took out his net, cast it, and drew it in, and found in it four fish, each one a different color.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَهُمْ الصَّيَّادُ فَرِحَ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْعِفْرِيتُ ادْخُلْ بِهِمْ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَ قَدِّمْهُمْ إِلَيْهِ فَإِنَّهُ يُعْطِيكَ مَا يُغْنِيكَ وَ بِاللَّهِ اقْبَلْ عُذْرِي فَإِنِّي فِي هٰذَا الْوَقْتِ لَمْ أَعْرِفْ طَرِيقًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾahum al-ṣayyādu fariḥa fa-qāla lahu al-ʿifrītu udkhul bihim ilā al-sulṭāni wa-qaddimhum ilayhi fa-innahu yuʿṭīka mā yughnīka wa-bi-Allāhi iqbal ʿudhrī fa-innī fī hādhā al-waqti lam aʿrif ṭarīqan
sentences.l: And when the fisherman saw them, he rejoiced; and the efrit said to him, 'Take them in to the Sultan, and present them to him, for he will give you what will content you. And, by God, accept my excuse, for at this time I know no way (to do more).'
sentences.i: When the fisherman saw them he was overjoyed; and the efrit said to him, 'Carry these in to the Sultan and present them to him, for he will reward you enough to satisfy you. And I beg you, by God, accept my excuse, for just now I can see no other course.'
sentences.n: لم اعرف طريقا is ambiguous: it may mean the efrit sees no way to reward the fisherman further himself (hence the referral to the Sultan), or, more darkly, that he still knows no way out of his own confinement — the reading is left open here as in the text.

sentences.t: وَ أَنَا فِي هٰذَا الْبَحْرِ مُدَّةَ أَلْفٍ وَ ثَمَانِمِايَةِ عَامٍ مَا رَأَيْتُ ظَاهِرَ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا فِي هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةِ وَ لَا تَصْطَادْ مِنْ هٰذِهِ الْبِرْكَةِ إِلَّا مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-anā fī hādhā al-baḥri muddata alfin wa-thamānimāyati ʿāmin mā raʾaytu ẕāhira al-dunyā illā fī hādhihi al-sāʿati wa-lā taṣṭād min hādhihi al-birkati illā marratan wāḥidatan kulla yawmin
sentences.l: And I have been in this sea for a period of one thousand and eight hundred years; I did not see the face of the world except in this hour. And you may not fish from this pool except once, a single time, every day.
sentences.i: I have lain in this sea for eighteen hundred years, and never once glimpsed the face of the world until this very hour. And from this pool you may fish only once each day.
sentences.n: ثمانمائة (eight hundred) is spelled here ثمانماية, with its medial hamza smoothed into a plain yāʾ, a defective spelling typical of this text's handling of medial hamzas.

sentences.t: وَ وَدَّعَهُ وَ قَالَ لَهُ لَا تُوحِشْنِي اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-waddaʿahu wa-qāla lahu lā tūḥishnī Allāhu
sentences.l: And he bade him farewell, and said to him, 'May God not make me desolate of you.'
sentences.i: Then he bade him farewell, saying, 'May God never bereave me of your company.'
sentences.n: لا توحشني الله is a set farewell blessing, literally 'may God not render me bereft/desolate of you' — a wish that they will meet again.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَقَّ الْأَرْضَ بِرِجْلِهِ فَانْشَقَّتِ الْأَرْضُ وَ بَلَعَتْهُ وَ مَضَى
sentences.tr: thumma daqqa al-arḍa bi-rijlihi fa-inshaqqati al-arḍu wa-balaʿathu wa-maḍā
sentences.l: Then he struck the earth with his foot, and the earth split open, and swallowed him, and he went away.
sentences.i: Then he struck the ground with his foot; the earth split apart, swallowed him up, and he was gone.

sentences.t: الصَّيَّادُ إِلَى المَدِينَةِ وَ هُوَ مُتَعَجِّبٌ مِمَّا جَرَى لَهُ مَعَ العِفْرِيتِ وَ كَيْفَ كَانَ
sentences.tr: al-ṣayyādu ilā al-madīnati wa-huwa mutaʿajjibun mimmā jarā lahu maʿa al-ʿifrīti wa-kayfa kāna
sentences.l: […continuing:] the fisherman, to the city, while he (was) astonished at what had happened to him with the efrit, and how it had been.
sentences.i: …on the fisherman went to the city, astonished at what had happened to him with the efrit, and how it had all come about.
sentences.n: This unit opens mid-sentence: its governing verb (likely 'he went,' resuming the fisherman's motion) belongs to the previous night's final clause, outside this excerpt.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ السَّمَكَ وَ دَخَلَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَ أَخَذَ مَاجُورًا ثُمَّ مَلَأَهُ مَاءًا وَ حَطَّ فِيهِ السَّمَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha al-samaka wa-dakhala ilā manzilihi wa-akhadha mājūran thumma malaʼahu māʼan wa-ḥaṭṭa fīhi al-samaka
sentences.l: Then he took the fish and entered into his house, and took a basin, then filled it with water, and put the fish into it.
sentences.i: Then he took the fish and went into his house; he took a large basin, filled it with water, and put the fish into it.
sentences.n: 'مَلَأَهُ' keeps the precomposed hamza-on-alif (أ) because the archive itself prints it so, in 'ملأه' — the one place in this slice where the edition uses a precomposed hamza rather than bare alif.

sentences.t: فَاخْتَبَطَ السَّمَكُ مِنْ دَاخِلِ المَاجُورِ فِي المَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-ikhtabaṭa al-samaku min dākhili al-mājūri fī al-māʼi
sentences.l: Then the fish thrashed about, from inside the basin, in the water.
sentences.i: Then the fish began to thrash about inside the basin, in the water.

sentences.t: وَ حَمَلَ المَاجُورَ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ وَ قَصَدَ بِهِ قَصْرَ المَلِكِ كَمَا أَمَرَهُ العِفْرِيتُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamala al-mājūra fawqa raʼsihi wa-qaṣada bihi qaṣra al-maliki kamā amarahu al-ʿifrītu
sentences.l: And he carried the basin above his head, and made, with it, for the palace of the king, as the efrit had commanded him.
sentences.i: He carried the basin on his head and set out with it for the king's palace, just as the efrit had ordered him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَ الصَّيَّادُ إِلَى المَلِكِ وَ قَدَّمَ لَهُ السَّمَكَ فَتَعَجَّبَ المَلِكُ غَايَةَ العَجَبِ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ السَّمَكِ الَّذِي قَدَّمَهُ الصَّيَّادُ وَلَا رَأَي فِي عُمْرِهِ صِفَةً وَ لَا شَكْلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿa al-ṣayyādu ilā al-maliki wa-qaddama lahu al-samaka fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku ghāyata al-ʿajabi min dhālika al-samaki alladhī qaddamahu al-ṣayyādu wa-lā raʼā fī ʿumrihi ṣifatan wa-lā shaklahu
sentences.l: Then when the fisherman went up to the king and presented to him the fish, the king marveled the utmost of marveling at that fish which the fisherman had presented — nor had he seen, in his life, a description of it, nor its shape.
sentences.i: So when the fisherman came before the king and presented the fish to him, the king marveled greatly at that fish the fisherman had brought — never in his life had he seen the like of it, in kind or in shape.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ المَلِكُ أَعْطُوا هٰذِهِ السَّمَكَ لِلْجَارِيَةِ الطَّبَّاخَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku aʿṭū hādhihi al-samaka li-al-jāriyati al-ṭabbākhati
sentences.l: Then the king said, 'Give this fish to the slave-girl, the cook.'
sentences.i: Then the king said, 'Give this fish to the girl who cooks.'
sentences.n: 'هٰذِهِ السَّمَكَ' uses the feminine demonstrative with al-samak, a noun ordinarily masculine collective in Classical Arabic (one expects هذا) — a non-Classical agreement, kept as printed.

sentences.t: قَٰلَ وَكَانَتْ هٰذِهِ الجَارِيَةُ أَهْدَاهَا لَهُ مَلِكُ الرُّومِ مُنْذُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَهُوَ لَمْ يُجَرِّبْهَا فِي طَبِيخٍ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-kānat hādhihi al-jāriyatu ahdāhā lahu maliku al-rūmi mundhu thalāthati ayyāmin wa-huwa lam yujarribhā fī ṭabīkhin
sentences.l: He said: and this slave-girl, the King of Rome had given her to him three days before, and he had not tried her out in cooking.
sentences.i: [Thus the tale resumes:] this girl had been given to him by the King of Rome three days earlier, and he had not yet tried her cooking.
sentences.n: The bare letters 'قل' printed in the archive here are the common defective spelling of 'قَالَ' — the narrator's standard resumptive tag after a quotation ('he/it is said') — pointed with the dagger alif (U+0670) rather than a full alif, per the edition's defective orthography.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الوَزِيرَ أَنْ تَقْلِيَهُنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-wazīra an taqliyahunna
sentences.l: So he commanded the vizier that she fry them.
sentences.i: So he ordered the vizier that the fish be fried.
sentences.n: The subordinate verb 'تَقْلِيَهُنَّ' has an implied feminine subject (she, i.e. the cook-girl) that does not match the stated object 'the vizier' — a compressed, elliptical construction (he ordered the vizier [to have her] fry them). The plural feminine object suffix -hunna treats the fish as feminine plural, unlike the singular feminine agreement in 'هٰذِهِ السَّمَكَ' and 'نَظَّفَتْهَا' elsewhere in this same episode.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَا جَارِيَهْ المَلِكُ يَقُولُ لَكِ مَا نَبْتَلِيكِ يَا دُمْعَتِي إِلَّا لِشِدَّتِي فَرِّحِينَا اليَوْمَ عَلَى صَنْعَتِكِ وَحُسْنِ طَبِيخِكِ وَأَنَّ السُّلْطَانَ أَنَى لَهُ وَاحِدٌ بِهَدِيَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yā jāriyatu al-maliku yaqūlu laki mā nabtalīki yā dumʿatī illā li-shiddatī farriḥīnā al-yawma ʿalā ṣanʿatiki wa-ḥusni ṭabīkhiki wa-anna al-sulṭāna anā lahu wāḥidun bi-hadiyyatin
sentences.l: So he said to her, 'O girl! The king says to you, We only test you, O my [teardrop?], except/save for my [hardship?] — so gladden us today with your skill and the goodness of your cooking; and that the Sultan, a man came to him with a gift.'
sentences.i: So he said to her, 'O girl, the king says to you: We only put you to the test, my dear, out of necessity — so delight us today with your skill and the excellence of your cooking, for a gift has come to the Sultan.'
sentences.n: Two obscure turns of phrase here: (1) 'يَا دُمْعَتِي' (lit. 'O my teardrop') and 'لِشِدَّتِي' ('for my hardship/need') — read as an endearment and a note of necessity, following evident sense rather than a secure parsing. (2) 'أَنَى لَهُ وَاحِدٌ بِهَدِيَّةٍ' — the printed passage explaining why the king wants the fish fried is compressed/possibly garbled; 'أَنَى' is read here as a variant of أتى/جاء ('to come'), vocalized on its bare letters rather than smoothed into standard grammar.

sentences.t: وَرَجَعَ الوَزِيرُ بَعْدَ مَا أَوْصَاهَا وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُعْطِيَ الصَّيَّادَ أَرْبَعَمَايَةَ دِينَارٍ فَأَعْطَاهُ الوَزِيرُ إِيَّاهَا
sentences.tr: wa-rajaʿa al-wazīru baʿda mā awṣāhā wa-amarahu an yuʿṭiya al-ṣayyāda arbaʿamāyata dīnārin fa-aʿṭāhu al-wazīru iyyāhā
sentences.l: And the vizier returned, after he had instructed her, and he [the king] had ordered him to give the fisherman four hundred dinars; so the vizier gave it to him.
sentences.i: The vizier went back after he had given her his instructions — for the king had ordered him to give the fisherman four hundred dinars — and the vizier gave him the money.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهَا فِي حُجْرَةٍ وَرَاحَ يَجْرِي إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَهُوَ يَقَعُ وَ يَقُومُ وَ يَعْثُرُ وَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّ ذٰلِكَ مَنَامًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahā fī ḥujratin wa-rāḥa yajrī ilā baytihi wa-huwa yaqaʿu wa-yaqūmu wa-yaʿthuru wa-yaẕunnu anna dhālika manāman
sentences.l: So he took it in a fold [of his garment], and went off running to his house, falling and rising and stumbling, thinking that this was a dream.
sentences.i: So he tucked it into the fold of his robe and went running home, falling, getting up, and stumbling, thinking it was all a dream.
sentences.n: 'حُجْرَةٍ' is read here as a fold or pocket of the garment (a common colloquial sense), rather than 'a room,' to fit the sense of tucking the money away as he ran.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اشْتَرَى لِعِيَالِهِ مَا يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَ دَخَلَ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ وَ هُوَ فَرْحَانٌ مَسْرُورٌ
sentences.tr: thumma ishtarā li-ʿiyālihi mā yaḥtājūna ilayhi wa-dakhala ʿalā zawjatihi wa-huwa farḥānun masrūrun
sentences.l: Then he bought for his family what they needed, and went in to his wife, joyful and glad.
sentences.i: Then he bought what his family needed and went in to his wife, joyful and delighted.

sentences.t: هٰذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الصَّيَّادِ وَ أَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الجَارِيَةِ فَإِنَّهَا أَخَذَتِ السَّمَكَ وَ نَظَّفَتْهَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-ṣayyādi wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-jāriyati fa-innahā akhadhati al-samaka wa-naẕẕafathā
sentences.l: This is what happened concerning the fisherman's affair; and as for what happened concerning the slave-girl's affair, she took the fish and cleaned them.
sentences.i: This is what happened with the fisherman. As for what happened with the girl — she took the fish and cleaned it.

sentences.t: وَ نَصَبَتِ الطَّاجِنَ ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَرْخَتِ السَّمَكَ فَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا اسْتَوَى وَجْهُهُ وَ قَلَبَتْهُ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ الثَّانِي
sentences.tr: wa-naṣabat al-ṭājina thumma innahā arkhat al-samaka fa-mā huwa illā istawā wajhuhu wa-qalabathu ʿalā al-wajhi al-thānī
sentences.l: And she set up the frying-pan; then indeed she let the fish down (into it); and no sooner had its face become done than she turned it onto the second face.
sentences.i: She set the pan on the fire and put the fish in; and no sooner had one side cooked than she turned it onto the other.
sentences.n: "ثم إنها" is a common narrative connective ("then indeed she..."), vocalised here with kasra (inna) rather than fatha (anna).

sentences.t: وَ إِذَا بِحَايِطِ الْمَطْبَخِ قَدِ إِنْشَقَّ وَ خَرَجَتْ مِنْهُ صَبِيَّةٌ مَلِيحَةُ الْقَدِّ أَسِيلَةُ الْخَدِّ كَحِيلَةُ الطَّرْفِ وَ هِيَ لَابِسَةٌ كُوفِيَّةَ حَرِيرٍ بِهُدَّابٍ أَزْرَقَ وَ فِي أُذُنَيْهَا حَلَقٌ وَ فِي مَعَاصِمِهَا زَوْجُ أَسَاوِرَ وَ فِي أَصَابِعِهَا خَوَاتِمُ بِالْفُصُوصِ الْجَوَاهِرِ الثَّمِينَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ḥāyiṭi al-maṭbakhi qad inshaqqa wa-kharajat minhu ṣabiyyatun malīḥatu al-qaddi asīlatu al-khaddi kaḥīlatu al-ṭarfi wa-hiya lābisatun kūfiyyata ḥarīrin bi-huddābin azraqa wa-fī udhunayhā ḥalaqun wa-fī maʿāṣimihā zawju asāwira wa-fī aṣābiʿihā khawātimu bi-al-fuṣūṣi al-jawāhiri al-thamīnati
sentences.l: And behold, the wall of the kitchen had split, and there came out of it a maiden, beautiful of stature, smooth of cheek, dark-eyed as with kohl; and she was wearing a silk kerchief with a blue fringe, and in her ears were rings, and on her wrists a pair of bracelets, and on her fingers rings with settings — precious jewels.
sentences.i: Suddenly the wall of the kitchen split open, and out of it came a maiden of lovely form, smooth-cheeked and dark-eyed, wearing a silk kerchief with a blue fringe; rings hung in her ears, a pair of bracelets circled her wrists, and on her fingers were rings set with precious stones.
sentences.n: "حايط" (wall) is spelled with ي rather than the hamza-seat of Classical "حائط", a colloquial pronunciation kept as printed. "بالفصوص الجواهر" strings two definite nouns without strict idafa marking — a loose Middle Arabic apposition, not corrected here.

sentences.t: وَ فِي يَدِهَا مِنَ الْخَيْزُرَانِ فَغَرَزَتِ الْقَضِيبَ فِي الطَّاجِنِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī yadihā mina al-khayzurāni fa-gharazat al-qaḍība fī al-ṭājini
sentences.l: and in her hand was [something] of cane; and she thrust the rod into the frying-pan
sentences.i: and in her hand was a wand of cane; and she thrust the rod into the pan
sentences.n: "من الخيزران" leaves the noun (the rod) unstated, supplied by "القضيب" in the clause that follows.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ يَا سَمَكُ أَنْتَ عَلَى الْعَهْدِ مُقِيمٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā samaku anta ʿalā al-ʿahdi muqīmun
sentences.l: and she said, "O fish, are you one who abides on the covenant?"
sentences.i: and she said, "O fish, are you keeping to the old covenant?"

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ ذَلِكَ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-jāriyatu dhālika ghushiya ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and when the girl saw that, it was drawn over her (i.e. she fainted)
sentences.i: When the girl saw that, she fainted.

sentences.t: وَ الصَّبِيَّةُ أَعَادَتِ الْقَوْلَ ثَانِيًا وَ ثَالِثًا
sentences.tr: wa-al-ṣabiyyatu aʿādati al-qawla thāniyan wa-thālithan
sentences.l: and the maiden repeated the saying a second time and a third time
sentences.i: and the maiden repeated her words a second time, and a third.

sentences.t: وَ السَّمَكُ شَالُوا رُؤُسَهُمْ مِنَ الطَّاجِنِ وَ قَالُوا بِلِسَانٍ فَصِيحٍ نَعَمْ نَعَمْ ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-samaku shālū ruʾūsahum mina al-ṭājini wa-qālū bi-lisānin faṣīḥin naʿam naʿam thumma anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: and the fish raised their heads out of the frying-pan and said, in eloquent tongue, "Yes, yes"; then it recited, saying:
sentences.i: and the fish raised their heads from the pan and cried, in clear speech, "Yes! Yes!" — then they recited these lines:
sentences.n: "شالوا" (raised/lifted) is colloquial for Classical "رفعوا", kept as a feature of the text. "السمك" (a collective) takes a plural verb here (شالوا، قالوا) but a singular one with "انشد" — the verb-number shifts within the same sentence, a Middle Arabic trait left uncorrected. "روسهم" is a defective spelling of "رؤوسهم" (their heads), the hamza-bearing واو contracted to one.

sentences.t: اِنْ عُلْتِ عُلْنَا وَاِنْ وَافَيْتِ وَافَيْنَا * وَاِنْ هَجَرْتِ فَاَنَا قَدْ تَهَافَيْنَا
sentences.tr: in ʿulti ʿulnā wa-in wāfayti wāfaynā * wa-in hajarti fa-anā qad tahāfaynā
sentences.l: If you sustained (us), we sustained (you); and if you kept faith, we kept faith; and if you forsook (us), then we have indeed collapsed/perished.
sentences.i: If you have stood by us, we have stood by you; if you kept faith, so have we; and should you forsake us, we shall surely be undone.
sentences.n: "عُلْتِ/عُلْنَا" are from the hollow verb "عَالَ يَعُولُ" ("to support, sustain a dependent"), not from "عَلَا" ("to rise") despite the resemblance — the given pointing (damma-sukūn, no wāw) confirms the hollow-verb reading. "تَهَافَيْنَا" (we threw ourselves down / rushed to ruin) rhymes against "وَافَيْنَا" (we kept faith), pairing constancy with self-destruction if forsaken.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْلَبَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ الطَّاجِنَ وَ خَرَجَتْ مِنْ مَوْضِعِ مَا أَتَتْ وَ الْتَأَمَ الْحَائِطُ كَمَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aqlabati al-ṣabiyyatu al-ṭājina wa-kharajat min mawḍiʿi mā atat wa-iltaʾama al-ḥāʾiṭu kamā kāna
sentences.l: Then at that, the maiden overturned the frying-pan, and went out from the place from which she had come, and the wall closed up as it had been.
sentences.i: At that, the maiden overturned the pan, went out the way she had come, and the wall closed up again as it had been.
sentences.n: Here "الحائط" (the wall) is spelled with its Classical hamza, unlike "حايط" earlier in the same passage — a scribal inconsistency kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَفَاقَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ مِنْ غَشْوَتِهَا فَرَأَتِ الْأَرْبَعَ سَمَكَاتٍ مُحْتَرِقِينَ مِثْلَ الْفَحْمِ الْأَسْوَدِ
sentences.tr: thumma afāqati al-jāriyatu min ghashwatihā fa-raʾati al-arbaʿa samakātin muḥtariqīna mithla al-faḥmi al-aswadi
sentences.l: Then the girl awoke from her swoon, and saw the four fish, burnt, like the black charcoal.
sentences.i: Then the girl came to from her faint, and saw the four fish burnt to black charcoal.
sentences.n: "محترقين" (burnt, masc. pl.) does not agree in gender with "سمكات" (fem. pl.) — another instance of the text's loose Middle Arabic concord, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مِنْ أَوَّلِ غَزَوَاتِهِ إِنْكَسَرَتْ عَصَانَهُ وَ وَقَعَتْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat min awwali ghazawātihi inkasarat ʿaṣānahu wa-waqaʿat ʿalā al-arḍi maghshiyyan ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and she said(?) — from the first of his raids(?), his staff(?) broke — and she fell to the ground, fainted.
sentences.i: — at the very first shock of it her strength gave way beneath her — and she fell to the ground in a swoon.
sentences.n: This clause is obscure and likely corrupt or garbled: "قالت" ("she said") introduces no quoted speech, and "غزواته"/"عصانه" ("his raids," "his staff") carry masculine suffixes with no antecedent "he," where the feminine girl is the expected referent. The evident sense, confirmed by what follows ("she fell to the ground fainted"), is that she lost her footing at the shock of the sight. A plausible candidate is a copyist's slip of "فقالت" for "فمالت" ("then she swayed/tottered"), with "ـه" here standing for the feminine suffix "ـها" (a known Middle Arabic orthographic habit) rather than a masculine "his." Rendered here by evident sense; the surface words are given literally above.

sentences.t: وَفِيمَا هِيَ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ إِذْ جَاءَ الْوَزِيرُ فَرَأَهَا الدَّرْدِيسَ لَا تَعْرِفُ السَّبْتَ مِنَ الْخَمِيسِ فَحَرَّكَهَا بِرِجْلِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-fīmā hiya ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli idh jāʾa al-wazīru fa-raʾāhā al-dardīsa lā taʿrifu al-sabta mina al-khamīsi fa-ḥarrakahā bi-rijlihi
sentences.l: And while she was in this state, when the vizier came, he saw her utterly dazed(?), not knowing Saturday from Thursday, so he stirred her with his foot.
sentences.i: And while she was in this state, the vizier came in; he found her utterly stupefied, not knowing Saturday from Thursday, so he nudged her with his foot.
sentences.n: "الدرديس" is obscure — possibly dialectal or corrupt; rendered here by evident sense ("utterly dazed/stupefied") rather than a specific known etymology. "لا تعرف السبت من الخميس" is a set idiom for total disorientation, given literally in l and idiomatically in i.

sentences.t: فَفَاقَتْ وَبَكَتْ وَأَعْلَمَتِ الْوَزِيرَ بِالْقِصَّهْ وَبِالَّذِي جَرَى فَتَعَجَّبَ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَالَ مَا هَذَا إِلَّا أَمْرٌ عَجِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-fāqat wa-bakat wa-aʿlamati al-wazīra bi-al-qiṣṣah wa-bi-al-ladhī jarā fa-taʿajjaba al-wazīru wa-qāla mā hādhā illā amrun ʿajībun
sentences.l: So she awoke, and wept, and informed the vizier of the story and of what had happened; and the vizier marvelled and said, "This is nothing but an astonishing matter."
sentences.i: She came to, and wept, and told the vizier the whole story and all that had happened; and the vizier marvelled, saying, "This is a strange matter indeed."
sentences.n: "القصه" is spelled with plain هـ rather than the expected ة — tāʾ marbūṭah written as hāʾ, a Middle Arabic/dialectal orthographic habit kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَرْسَلَ خَلْفَ الصَّيَّادِ فَأَتَوْا بِهِ فَصَرَخَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الصَّيَّادُ جِي لَنَا أَرْبَعَ سَمَكَاتٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu arsala khalfa al-ṣayyādi fa-ataw bihi fa-ṣarakha ʿalayhi al-wazīru wa-qāla lahu ayyuhā al-ṣayyādu jī lanā arbaʿa samakātin
sentences.l: Then indeed he sent after the fisherman, and they brought him; and the vizier cried out at him and said to him, "O fisherman, bring us four fish."
sentences.i: Then he sent for the fisherman, and they brought him in; and the vizier shouted at him, "You there, fisherman — bring us four fish!"
sentences.n: "جي" is a Middle Arabic imperative form of "جاء/جيء" ("come"/"bring"), kept as printed rather than normalised to Classical "جِئْ".

sentences.t: مِثْلَ الَّذِي جِئْتَ بِهَا
sentences.tr: mithla al-ladhī jiʾta bihā
sentences.l: the like of that which you brought (f.)
sentences.n: This half-line completes the vizier's demand from the sentence before this slice's archived span ("bring me four more like the ones you brought"); its opening words are not part of this excerpt.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الصَّيَّادُ إِلَى الْبِرْكَةِ وَطَرَحَ الشَّبَكَةَ جَذَبَهَا وَ إِذَا بِأَرْبَعِ سَمَكَاتٍ مِثْلِهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ وَجَابَهُمْ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-ṣayyādu ilā al-birkati wa-ṭaraḥa al-shabakata jadhabahā wa-idhā bi-arbaʿi samakātin mithlihim fa-akhadhahum wa-jābahum ilā al-wazīri
sentences.l: So the fisherman went out to the pool and cast the net, drew it in, and behold, four fish like them; so he took them and brought them to the vizier.
sentences.i: So the fisherman went out to the pool, cast his net, and drew it in — and there were four fish just like the first! He took them and brought them to the vizier.
sentences.n: جَذَبَهَا follows without a connecting wa- in the source (asyndeton). مِثْلِهِمْ takes the masculine plural pronoun -him for the feminine plural سَمَكَات ‘fish’, a gender-agreement laxity typical of this text. وَجَابَهُمْ is a colloquial/Middle Arabic verb for ‘brought them’, not the Classical جاء بهم construction.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ بِهِمُ الْوَزِيرُ إِلَى الْجَارِيَةِ وَقَالَ لَهَا قُومِي اِقْلِبِيهِمْ قُدَّامِي حَتَّى أَرَى عَلَيْهَا الْقَضِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala bihimu al-wazīru ilā al-jāriyati wa-qāla lahā qūmī iqlibīhim quddāmī ḥattā arā ʿalayhā al-qaḍiyyata
sentences.l: So the vizier went in with them to the slave-girl and said to her, ‘Arise, turn them over before me, that I may see the matter for myself.’
sentences.i: The vizier brought them in to the slave-girl and said to her, ‘Get up and fry them in front of me, so that I may witness it with my own eyes.’
sentences.n: اِقْلِبِيهِمْ, literally ‘turn them over’, is used for frying, as earlier in this scene.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَأَصْلَحَتْهُمْ وَعَلَّقَتِ الطَّاجِنَ وَطَرَحَتْهُمْ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmati al-jāriyatu wa-aṣlaḥat-hum wa-ʿallaqati al-ṭājina wa-ṭaraḥat-hum fīhi
sentences.l: So the slave-girl arose, and prepared them, and hung up the frying-pan, and put them into it.
sentences.i: The slave-girl got up, cleaned the fish, set the pan on the fire, and put them in.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اِسْتَقَرَّ السَّمَكُ فِي الطَّاجِنِ إِلَّا وَالْحَائِطُ قَدِ اِنْشَقَّ وَالصَّبِيَّةُ ظَهَرَتْ وَهِيَ فِي هَيْئَتِهَا الْأُولَى وَفِي يَدِهَا الْقَضِيبُ فَغَرَزَتْهُ فِي الطَّاجِنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqarra al-samaku fī al-ṭājini illā wa-al-ḥāʾiṭu qadi inshaqqa wa-al-ṣabiyyatu ẓaharat wa-hiya fī hayʾatihā al-ūlā wa-fī yadihā al-qaḍību fa-gharazat-hu fī al-ṭājini
sentences.l: Then when the fish had settled in the pan, behold, the wall had split, and the maiden appeared, she being in her former shape, and in her hand the wand; and she thrust it into the pan.
sentences.i: No sooner had the fish settled in the pan than the wall split open and the maiden appeared, just as she had before, wand in hand, and she thrust it into the pan.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا ... إِلَّا وَ... is an idiomatic narrative construction meaning ‘no sooner had X happened than Y’.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا سَمَكُ يَا سَمَكُ أَنْتُمْ عَلَى الْعَهْدِ الْقَدِيمِ مُقِيمٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā samaku yā samaku antum ʿalā al-ʿahdi al-qadīmi muqīmun
sentences.l: And she said, ‘O fish, O fish, are you upon the old covenant remaining?’
sentences.i: She said, ‘O fish, O fish, do you still hold to the old covenant?’
sentences.n: مُقِيمٌ is singular though its subject أَنْتُمْ is plural — a number-agreement laxity typical of this text's Middle Arabic register.

sentences.t: وَ إِذَا بِالسَّمَكِ الْجَمِيعِ قَدْ شَالُوا رُؤُسَهُمْ وَقَالُوا هَذَا الْبَيْتُ السَّابِقُ وَهُوَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-samaki al-jamīʿi qad shālū ruʾūsahum wa-qālū hādhā al-baytu al-sābiqu wa-huwa
sentences.l: And behold, all the fish had raised their heads and said, ‘This is the previous verse, and it is:’
sentences.i: And all at once, every one of the fish lifted its head and said, ‘This is the same verse as before — and it is:’
sentences.n: رُؤوسَهُمْ (‘their heads’) is spelled defectively in the source (رؤسهم, without the plene و of the standard plural رؤوس).

sentences.t: اِنْ عُدْتِ عُدْنَا وَاِنْ وَافَيْتِ وَافَيْنَا * وَاِنْ هَجَرْتُمْ قَدْ فَانَا تَدْفَيْنَا
sentences.tr: in ʿudti ʿudnā wa-in wāfayti wāfaynā * wa-in hajartum qad fānā tadfaynā
sentences.l: If you return, we return; and if you keep faith, we keep faith — and if you (all) forsook (us), then we ... would have warmed one another.
sentences.i: If you come back, we come back to you; if you are true, we are true; and were you to forsake us, we would — it seems — have kept each other warm in your absence.
sentences.n: This couplet repeats the fish's first verse (given earlier in the night, not in this slice) with variation: عُدْتِ/عُحْنَا replaces عُلْتِ/عُلْنَا, and the second hemistich has the plural هَجَرْتُمْ ‘you (all) forsook’ ... تَدْفَيْنَا where the earlier verse had singular هَجَرْتِ ... تَهَافَيْنَا. تَدْفَيْنَا would derive from د-ف-ا/د-ف-أ ‘to grow warm’ (i.e. ‘we would keep each other warm’), but its close resemblance to تَهَافَيْنَا ‘we would perish/rush together’ suggests a compositor's corruption or rearrangement of the same rhyme-word rather than a deliberate new reading. The precise sense is accordingly uncertain; it is vocalized and translated here exactly as printed, without silently conforming it to the earlier verse's wording.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: Morning overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent from lawful speech.
